page: Amazon Web Services m5d.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled as 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store, and network performance is anchored by a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25%. However, the massive core count enables strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench ray tracing benchmarks ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 4503.76 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 214.54 GB/sec.

The inclusion of 3600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage combined with strong multi-threaded capabilities makes this instance highly suitable for database operations, high-throughput web serving, and multi-threaded data processing. Redis SET operations perform exceptionally well, reaching 74.41 million operations per second. While single-threaded tasks and LLM text generation are weak points, the high resource density and bundled local storage offer a cost-effective profile for workloads requiring balanced compute, memory, and fast local temporary storage without the overhead of network-attached storage.
